why: The documented skip, measured. `typescript_extractor.py` states that instance calls on a typed variable are deliberately not emitted because they would need type inference, and that a guessed edge poisons grounding. This case puts a recall number on that stance, across both shapes it applies to: a call through an annotated parameter, and a call through a local whose type is obvious from `new`.
excluded: `this.format()` inside `run` is NOT excluded — the front-end documents `this.method()` to a sibling as resolved, so it is labelled and expected to match. It is the control within this case.

The `known_gaps` this case carried are gone, and not because they were waived: the front-end learned to emit every edge they named, so each entry had become an assertion that a limitation still existed when it did not. Found 2026-09-21 by the check added alongside — a gap naming an edge the extractor now emits fails the case to load, the same way a broken `refusal` does. Until then load-time validation only asked whether the gap named an edge in `edges`, which a closed gap still satisfies.
resolved_by_measurement: Construction is a CROSS-LANGUAGE INCONSISTENCY, and this is a real recall gap rather than a vocabulary error. Python emits `caller -CALLS-> Type` for `Item(name)`; TypeScript emits nothing for `new Handler()`. The vocabulary supports the edge — the same `CALLS` kind, the same `Type` node — so the TS front-end is behind Python here, not modelling something different. Kept in `edges` as a miss and moved into `known_gaps` below.
